sentences.text: 7.Final Order Accused is acquitted.
8.Date of Order 13/03/2024.
JUDGMENT

The Police Sub-Inspector of Upparpete Police Station, Bengaluru has filed this charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable U/Sec.51(1)(b), 63 of Copyright Act and section 420 of IPC.
02.

The brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:
It is the case of the prosecution that, on 03.08.2017 at about 4.30 pm within the limits of Upperpet Police station, situated at Vinay Enterprises, Gandhi Nagar,
Opposite to Tribhuvan talkies, Burma Bazaar, Bengaluru.

The accused manufacturing of spurious/ counterfeit rechargeable batteries, cameras, belts, lens caps and chargers of NIKON Company of CW.5 without obtaining any permission from CW.5 and was selling the duplicate rechargeable batteries, cameras, belts, lens caps and chargers to the public and cheated the company and public and thereby violated the copyright of the company

. In this regard, CW.5 lodged first information statement and based on the same FIR came to be registered in Cr.No.157/2017 for the offence punishable U/Sec.51(1)(b), 63 of Copyright Act and section 420 of IPC.
Thereafter, CW.5 along with CW.1 to 3 and with panchas rushed to the spot and conducted raid and seized the alleged duplicate products by drawing panchanama.

Thereafter, PI completed the investigation and filed the charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable U/Sec.51(1)(b), 63 of Copyright Act and section 420 of IPC.
03.

After filing of the charge sheet this Court has taken the cognizance of the offences punishable under section U/Sec.51(1)(b), 63 of Copyright Act and section 420 of IPC and issued summons to the accused.
Accused has appeared before this Court through his counsel and obtained bail.
The copy of the charge sheet has been furnished to the accused as per Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.
After hearing both sides the charge has been framed and read over to accused.
But, he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Hence, the case has been posted for prosecution evidence.

04. The prosecution in order to prove its case, has examined witnesses as PW.1 to 3 and documents got marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 and one material object as per MO.1 and closed the side of the prosecution evidence and Statements u/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. recorded, read over and explained in the vernacular language of the accused, wherein accused have denied the incriminating circumstances appeared against him as false and did not choose to lead defence evidence.
05. I have heard the arguments of both sides.
Perused the entire oral evidence and documents placed on record.

06. The points that arise for my consideration are as under:

sentences.text: (1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on 03.08.2017 at about 4.30 pm within the limits of Upperpet Police station, situated at Vinay Enterprises, Gandhi Nagar, Opposite to Tribhuvan talkies, Burma Bazaar, Bengaluru.

The accused manufacturing of spurious/ counterfeit rechargeable batteries, cameras,
belts, lens caps and chargers of NIKON Company of CW.5 without obtaining any permission from CW.5 and was selling the duplicate rechargeable batteries, cameras,
belts, lens caps and chargers to the public and cheated the company and public and thereby violated the copyright of the company and thereby have committed alleged offence punishable U/Sec.51(1)(b), 63 of Copyright Act and section 420 of IPC. ?
(2) What order ?

07. My findings to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Negative, Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following :
REASONS 08. Point No.1 :- It is well settled that in a criminal case the entire burden of proof rests upon the prosecution and the accused need to prove nothing.
Suffice for the accused to create doubt about the case of the prosecution and the reliability of the witnesses for the prosecution.

09. The prosecution has alleged that, on 03.08.2017 at about 4.30 pm within the limits of Upparpet Police station, situated at Vinay Enterprises, Gandhi Nagar, Opposite to Tribhuvan talkies, Burma Bazaar, Bengaluru.

The accused manufacturing of spurious/ counterfeit rechargeable batteries,
cameras, belts, lens caps and chargers of NIKON Company of CW.5 without obtaining any permission from CW.5 and was selling the duplicate rechargeable batteries, cameras, belts, lens caps and chargers to the public and cheated the company and public and thereby violated the copyright of the company and thereby have committed alleged offence punishable U/Sec.51(1)(b), 63 of Copyright Act and section 420 of IPC.
Therefore, the burden is on the prosecution to prove guilt of the accused.

As already stated supra, the prosecution has examined 3 witnesses as PW.1 to PW.3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7.
10.
The prosecution has been examined CW.7 as PW.1, he being Police Officer and partial Investigation Officer of this case.
He specifically testified before this court that, on 04.08.2017, he received this case file from CW.1, he had been proceed to conduct further investigation.
That on 18.01.2019, he sent seized sample articles to Manager Nikon India Private Limited, SR Nagara and requested to issue genuinity certificate.
Further, he deposed before the court that, he received report from manager Nikon India Private Limited, SR Nagara.
He identified MO.1 and Ex.P. 1 & 2 documents.
After that, he charge sheeted against accused and he identified accused.
He has been subjected by cross examination by accused.
11. The prosecution has been examined CW.6 as PW.2, she being Police Officer.

She specifically testified before this court that, on 03.08.2017, when she was on station house officer duty, CW.1 Umashankar B, Pi vs Rajesh Kumar on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17148638/
3 came and gave written complaint, verify and registered case and she prepared FIR, original copy of FIR submitted before Jurisdictional trial court and copy of FIR forwarded to his Police Officers.

After that, she handed over this case file in view of the order passed by Commissioner of Police,
Bengaluru to CCB for further investigation.
She has been subjected by cross examination by accused.
12. The prosecution has been examined CW.4 as PW.3, he being Police Officer and associate with CW.1 while conduct raid.

He specifically testified before the court that, on 03.08.2017, when he was on duty, CW. 1 called to his chamber and informed about counterfeit Nikon company spare parts selling in Barma Bazar, Gandhi Nagara, Bengaluru.
Accordingly, they had been to Vinay Enterprises Shop, Barma Bazar, Thribhuvan Theator, Gandhinagara, Bengaluru.

Further, he deposed before the court that, at the time of leave of CCB Office, CW.1 called two panchas, then they have went to the Vinay Enterprises shop and found one person Rajesh Kumar, he himself stated before CW.1 , he is the owner of said shop.
After verification of shop by CW.1, he found counterfeit products of Nikon Company Battery, belts, lens cap, charges.
CW.1 has seized the said spare parts by drawing Ex.P.5 in the presence of two panchas, Police Officers and accused.
Panchas and accused have signed on Ex.P.5 in his presence, he is also signed on Ex.P.5 at accused's shop.
After that, CW. 1 took seized articles and accused and came back to CCB Office, he gave statement before Investigation Officer and he identified accused and MO's.
He has been subjected cross examination by accused.
13. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence placed by prosecution it appears that, it is the suo-moto case registered by CW.1 on 03.08.2017.

Further, it appears from Ex.P.3, the ACP CCB (F&
M) has got credible information regarding selling of similar products of reputed company Nikon and stored at Vinay Enterprises, camera and flashes No.19B, Barma Bazar, opposite to Thribhuvan Theartor, Gandhinagara, Bengaluru-09.
CW.1 has been directed by ACP CCB (F& M) to verify information received by him and if found any merits and he has been directed to take necessary legal action against the owner of said shop.
Accordingly, CW.1 went to the said shop and found the shop owner has stored and selling reputed company i.e., Nikon counterfeit products of charger and other mobile accessories.
Therefore, he gave FIS before SHO of Upparpete Police Station.
Further, it appears from materials that, CW.1 and his team have raid on accused's shop without register FIR.
After seized mobile accessories from accused, CW.1 and his team went to SHO of Upparpete Police Station and handed over seized articles, accused, mahazar and self report of CW.1 to CW.6.

But,
CW.6 deposed in her chief examination, she only received written complaint of CW.1, she is not whisper anything about mahazar, accused , seized articles.

Further, in her cross examination, she clearly admitted that, she is not took signature of CW.1 in Ex.P.4 column No.12, it is mandatory under law to give copy of FIR to informant at free of cost and the Police Officers should take signature of informant in FIR column NO.12.
But, in the instant case, this mandatory directions has not been complied.
So, it appears that, CW.1 not yet went to the SHO of Upparpete Police Station and it is doubtful handed over seized articles, mahazar, accused and complaint to CW.6.

Further, it appears from prosecution papers, as per the evidence of PW.1, on 18.01.2019, he sent sample articles to Manager, Nikon India Private Limited and requested to issue genuinity certificate and he received certificate from company Manager.

As per Ex.P.5, CW.1 seized some counterfeit Nikon Company mobile accessories i.e., Nikon Company duplicate rechargeable battery - 93 , Nikon Company duplicate camera belt-27, Nikon Company duplicate lens cap - 60, Nikon Company duplicate Umashankar B, Pi vs Rajesh Kumar on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17148638/
4 charger- 41 and out of which, CW.1 has separated one each as a sample and sealed in the presence of panchas.

Further, it appears from Ex.P.2 reply letter from Nikon Company Manager, in the below table we have provided the result of our examination on the sample articles containing " Nikon" mark that were shared by you;
SL.NO.
Product Qty Status 1. EN-EL9 3 Counterfeit 2. EN-EL3e 1 We cannot be 100% certain 3. MH-25 1 Counterfeit 4. MH-24 1 Counterfeit 5. Strap 3 We cannot be 100% certain
6. Lens front  cap 55 mm 3 Counterfeit 7
. MH-18a 1 Counterfeit

Further, it is clear CW.7 has sent seized articles to company officials as per Ex.P.1 and as per the Ex.P.5, CW.1 has separated one each sample product from seized articles, but in Ex.P.2, three items found 3 in numbers.

So, from Ex.P.2, it appears that,
CW.7 has not sent seized articles of this case.
Further, Ex.P.2 does not contain the name of person who conduct technical analysis over sample articles.

Further, it appears from prosecution papers,
there is no any materials to send original product of Nikon Company for technical analysis.

Further,
it is relevant to note that, despite took coercive steps against CW.1 to 3 and 5, the prosecution has failed to secure their presence well in time,
Therefore, this court took prayer of Learned Senior APP and CW.1 to 3 and 5 are dropped out vide order dated 30.01.2024.
CW.1 and panch witness are material witnesses, they have not stepped into witness box.
So, non examination of material witnesses is fatal to the case of prosecution.
The prosecution has not proved contents and recovery of counterfeit products as alleged in Ex.P.5 beyond all reasonable doubts.
The evidence of PW.1 to 3 has many discrepancies and this evidence has creates serious doubt and PW.1 to 3 evidence has not corroborate with independent evidence.
Therefore, this court came to clear conclusion that, the prosecution has been failed to prove guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the negative.
14. Point No.2:

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
